guitar.modelsText: G&L Rampage (early) / Gibson Les Paul (signature model)
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Cantrell is well documented playing a G&L Rampage in early Alice in Chains years, later closely associated with Gibson Les Paul (his own signature model).
guitar.notes: Original entry correct and well documented.

tone.target: nasal heavy fuzz-crunch grunge with thick low mids
tone.profile: nasal heavy fuzz-crunch grunge with thick low mids
tone.summary: A fuzzy signal chain starting with a Muff-style fuzz, followed by an OD boost to shape the mids, driving a British high-gain amp model (UK 45) into a robust cabinet (UK Vintage 4x12).

rig.name: Alice in Chains - Angry Chair - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and noise inherent in heavy fuzz tones.
Provide the core fuzzy sustain and dark, thick texture required for grunge.
Shove the low-mids and increase overall output volume for maximum crunch.
blocks.gap: Using Boost to simulate a mid-hump pedal (like an EQ boost) is necessary to achieve the 'low-mid shove' without dedicated EQ placement here.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall-ish high-gain breakup and classic rock tone foundation.
Provide a robust, classic British cabinet sound to complement the high-gain amp.
Sculpt the tone by emphasizing low-mids and cutting excessive high frequencies to achieve a darker sound.
Placeholder block. Modulation is avoided per the 'avoid' list.
blocks.gap: The Chorus module is included as a required modulation slot, but disabled to meet the tone requirements.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for darker, thicker cabinet realism.

proposals.reason: Enhance the dark, thick low-mids required for grunge tone.
